---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. An unresolved critical business fact blocks affected modeling; implementation convenience is not evidence.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. It contains the authoritative TODO/Gate process, full normal-development CLI map, project boundaries, phase rules, required reference routing, Runtime acceptance, and terminal policy. Follow every applicable routed reference it requires. A full batch reads the whole guide; a light batch may omit only TODO sections under the guide's explicit light-batch rules, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |
| complete TODO, Gate first-execution receipts, and session ownership | [session TODO and Gate receipts](references/development-guide.md#session-todo-and-gate-receipts) |
| project ownership and frontend finding routing | [project and frontend boundaries](references/development-guide.md#project-and-frontend-boundaries) |
| requirements extraction and critical ambiguity | [requirements to domain facts](references/development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts) |
| domain truth, settlement, list Report, and technical prevention Gates | [domain truth design](references/development-guide.md#domain-truth-design) |
| capability reconciliation and metadata modeling | [model and capability mapping](references/development-guide.md#model-and-capability-mapping) |
| declarative authoring and the only release command | [model apply is the only release](references/development-guide.md#model-apply-is-the-only-release) |
| bounded installed-batch Action context | [source prepare implementation packet](references/development-guide.md#source-prepare-implementation-packet) |
| valid check, source finalize, focused tests, and exact receipts | [project check to finalize to tests](references/development-guide.md#project-check-to-finalize-to-tests) |
| semantic journey binding and highest-risk canary | [semantic execution and canary](references/development-guide.md#semantic-execution-and-canary) |
| managed Runtime and exact-denominator acceptance | [Runtime and acceptance](references/development-guide.md#runtime-and-acceptance) |
| evidence ceiling and terminal states | [done terminal policy](references/development-guide.md#done-terminal-policy) |
| initial credential and acceptance-identity safety | [system seed login](references/development-guide.md#system-seed-login) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Its reviewed `--product-surfaces` value is an integration boundary, never frontend mutation authorization. Repair reported model/input failures and rerun the same command; never split publication/materialization or bypass destructive/evolution review.
- Every check, finalize, and focused-test command must run through its own Gate on its first real execution. Never run it directly first, rerun merely to obtain evidence, search historical receipts, or attach another command's receipt. A receipt proves only its original Gate and current bound identities; changed bound source/model/Runtime/artifact content makes it stale.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success.
- After current source finalization and focused tests pass, run one highest-risk semantic canary across formal identity/context resolution → command → persisted effect → actor-visible read-back before broad Runtime integration. A canary failure blocks dependents and is repaired once at its owner; it never shrinks the frozen model or acceptance denominator.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

item.aggregated_output: # Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. Domainry Plane exposes backend capability contracts plus the transport-only `@domainry/runtime-client` the frontend consumes; Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source stays read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [runtime-client.md](runtime-client.md) for the client contract the frontend binds against. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` route is selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. It never loads this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; its compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, session ID, TODO, compact `resume_packet`, one-time `authoring_context`, routed reference paths, and package identity to the result. `DOMAINRY_CLI` must equal the same package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. Never resolve a CLI through `PATH`, substitute another Skill, or call Domainry Plane directly. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. These actions are setup rather than stages or TODO gates. Use only the applicable command families below, in TODO order. Add one pinned `--environment ` or `--service ` target wherever shown and keep it consistent. Use `--help` only to resolve listed-command flags; do not invent neighboring commands. The packaged CLI has no update, sync, doctor, audit, repair, rollback, migration, or generic contract-search surface. ```text # initialization and SDK bootstrap "$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project materialize runtime-client --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [target] # fixed capability discovery "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-categories --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-category --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key # complete declarative model, inspection, and one-time legacy bootstrap "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # the only release command; an existing delivery may require its emitted evolution review "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] [--allow-destructive] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] --evolution-audit-sha256 --evolution-reason # approved source gaps "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] ... "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action source apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] ... --input - "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector definition --json [target] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ... # source closure in this exact order before developer tests "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project check --json --scope actions --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # verification, package, managed Runtime, and exact acceptance denominator "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process start --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --bundle --address 127.0.0.1: "$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process status --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ``` The only current managed project-state root is the stable `.domainry/builder/**`. The first valid Builder project command uses `domainry-builder-state-root-migration-v1` to discover and atomically rename any single real legacy `.domainry/builder-*` root under the cross-version project mutation lock. The CLI refuses to merge or overwrite whenever more than one current/legacy root exists, rejects symlink or non-directory roots, and normalizes only persisted path-valued JSON prefixes while preserving protocol/history strings. Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate any managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability. Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them. This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence. Use this precedence when evidence conflicts: 1. explicit current user decision; 2. latest accepted requirement or design contract; 3. latest implemented frontend behavior; 4. typed API and Mock semantics; 5. frontend tests; 6. legacy/reference implementation. Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract at least: - pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success; - canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination; - commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects; - roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior; - validation, stable errors, conflicts, optimistic concurrency, transaction boundaries, idempotency, and replay behavior; - calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior; - schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects; - presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata. Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof. Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures. ### Resolve critical ambiguity Do not infer any unresolved object identity, financial or payroll formula, permission boundary, state transition, inventory effect, or external side effect. Keep the affected requirement and downstream modeling items blocked until the user or accepted requirement evidence confirms the rule. A visual button, fixture value, label, or legacy endpoint proves demand exists but does not prove the business rule. Non-critical open items may proceed only when the PRD records the assumption, decision owner, fallback, and excluded acceptance scope. Finish the round before repair, then batch-repair by owner group and re-run the invalidated backend checks until no open finding remains (Round discipline). ## verify After the backend converges, read [evidence-levels.md](evidence-levels.md) and [verification.md](verification.md) completely and re-read [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md). `project verify` and packaging prove `delivery_verified` structural/release closure, not `scenario_verified` real-data behavior. Run the complete verify check-and-evidence inventory specified in verification — source boundary, backend/frontend suites, checklist/live validation, verify + package, managed Runtime, acceptance denominator prepare/harness/check, authorization/data-scope/idempotency journeys, matrix consistency, long/dense cases, and cleanup. Guide-specific ordering rules: - validate that the source-finalization receipt is still current; if source changes during repair, return to finalization before compiling or testing; - confirm the persisted Action/permission and role/effective-menu matrices still match the restarted Runtime and accepted database. After the matching managed Runtime is healthy, run `project acceptance prepare`, then execute the platform runner **first** with `project acceptance run --cases standard` and inspect its exact-set v2 result rows. Build business harness assertions on `assets/acceptance-harness-core.py` only for `state:"not_passed"` rows with `disposition:"needs_business_harness"`. Repair `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, or `runtime_failed` at the named owner before rerunning. Then run `project acceptance check`. Every assertion obtains its session through `harness.session_for_case(case)`, uses `ScenarioGraph` for isolated setup/dependencies, and applies `ReasonOracle` for the declared status/error/state/audit/positive-control reason; never select a user from a role name, create profile headers, or read an internal identity table. The denominator is CLI-owned and never hand-edited. After a model evolution, run `project acceptance stale-report` and re-record only reported `stale`/`missing` cases, never the full set. Prose, arbitrary hashed text, or a coverage percentage cannot replace the harness. Record the whole verify round before repair. If any finding exists, return it to its model or implementation owner, repair the batch, and run verify again (Round discipline). ## done Record exactly one terminal state from [verification.md](verification.md): `done`, `acceptance_failed`, or `verification_blocked`, applying its failure classification and terminal policy. `done` requires every in-scope TODO item closed with concise current evidence, an empty finding inventory, a passing final verify round, every in-scope requirement mapped to implemented source and current validation evidence, and no requirement or limitation hidden, downgraded, or deferred. Product prerequisites such as identities, data, permissions, Runtime health, or persistence are implementation/Foundation defects, not environmental blockers. Do not claim `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done` above the highest evidence level reached; no structural pass upgrades delivery evidence into real-data behavior. For any terminal state, require the applicable `verify` and `done` Gate status, close every finding according to the terminal policy, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` immediately before the final response. Repair inconsistency and rerun until it passes. This linter pass is not test, Runtime, delivery, or scenario evidence. Provide a concise completion summary with implemented scope, test results, Runtime results, and explicitly non-blocking limitations. ## System seed login Runtime owns every initial credential. Never write credential rows, embed a password in model/source/TODO/evidence, or replace formal provisioning and password-change flows. A missing system/project seed credential is initialized from Runtime's deployment-owned `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`; production startup rejects the built-in development value and the credential is always marked `must_change_password:true`. A user created through the formal Identity API receives a cryptographically random per-user password exactly once in a `Cache-Control: no-store` response and must change it. Startup fills only a missing credential; it never overwrites an existing password hash, clears a lock, or undoes a changed password. The canonical system identity is user ID `admin`, login `admin@example.com`, Admin Console `/admin`, Surface `admin_console`. In a managed development Runtime started by this workflow, a deployment without `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` seeds every missing credential — `admin` and project-declared acceptance identities — with development default `Domainry@2026`, marked `must_change_password:true`; production rejects this value. Establish a managed-development acceptance session by logging in with that default, completing forced change through `POST /auth/change-password` with `Idempotency-Key`, and keeping the new credential only in authorized secret handoff. Never print credentials into evidence or guess passwords: five failed logins produce `auth.account_locked`, and expiry does not lift the lock; an admin session must call `POST /identity/users/{userID}/unlock`. Formal Identity API users instead use their one-time no-store password. Business Workspace and Consumer Portal actors come from project-declared non-human acceptance identities. Authentication mode, session refresh, and authorization are independent of Surface; protected operations still enforce functional permission, ownership, Action policy, assurance, and data scope.

"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ``` The only current managed project-state root is the stable `.domainry/builder/**`. The first valid Builder project command uses `domainry-builder-state-root-migration-v1` to discover and atomically rename any single real legacy `.domainry/builder-*` root under the cross-version project mutation lock. The CLI refuses to merge or overwrite whenever more than one current/legacy root exists, rejects symlink or non-directory roots, and normalizes only persisted path-valued JSON prefixes while preserving protocol/history strings. Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate any managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability. Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them. This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence. Use this precedence when evidence conflicts: 1. explicit current user decision; 2. latest accepted requirement or design contract; 3. latest implemented frontend behavior; 4. typed API and Mock semantics; 5. frontend tests; 6. legacy/reference implementation. Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract at least: - pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success; - canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination; - commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects; - roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior; - validation, stable errors, conflicts, optimistic concurrency, transaction boundaries, idempotency, and replay behavior; - calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior; - schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects; - presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata. Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof. Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures. ### Resolve critical ambiguity Do not infer any unresolved object identity, financial or payroll formula, permission boundary, state transition, inventory effect, or external side effect. Keep the affected requirement and downstream modeling items blocked until the user or accepted requirement evidence confirms the rule. A visual button, fixture value, label, or legacy endpoint proves demand exists but does not prove the business rule. Non-critical open items may proceed only when the PRD records the assumption, decision owner, fallback, and excluded acceptance scope. Never mark them `confirmed` merely because implementation is possible. ## domain truth design Read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) completely. Freeze the domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement; close every calculation's ownership/persistence/correction decisions per that document. A capability is an implementation option after these facts exist; it is not evidence for choosing them. Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts must remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, model the write-side atomic Action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its Reports. Keep every affected model item blocked until this Gate closes. ### Mandatory list Report and export Gate Before discovering or selecting a Report capability, close every applicable contract below as a blocking design and acceptance Gate: 1. **List Report pagination:** every list Report has bounded server pagination: platform standard or `page_size` plus opaque cursor, maximum page size 200, stable ordering with a unique cursor tie-breaker, explicit `truncated`, and `total_semantics` of `exact` or `at_least`. A transport page that materializes the complete result before slicing is not bounded execution. 2. **Same-Report threshold routing:** export prepare makes one bounded probe of the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed threshold is 1000: an exhausted `0..1000` probe yields the exact total and one synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 immediately routes to the platform asynchronous paged export-job substrate, whose terminal result records the final exact total. Both branches use the identical Report/SQL/source hash/parameters/Scope; no count-only or export-only second query is allowed. 3. **Asynchronous reauthorization and terminal notification:** before asynchronous page one, the worker reconstructs the current persisted project user-role principal in the frozen workspace and compares canonical authorization Scope, failing closed on real drift. It never substitutes a manifest-only role or synthetic Surface. Only this branch publishes requester-only `completed`/`failed` Inbox notifications linked through export job, audit, and artifact. 4. **Atomic fingerprint replay:** the server canonicalizes Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and result version. Equivalent requests atomically reuse an accepted/running job or a completed unexpired artifact without a second file, download record, or terminal notification. `audit_id` stays out of the fingerprint; only failed/cancelled work or expired/corrupt artifacts may create one new execution through database compare-and-create. Require `pagination_trace`, a signed cursor strategy, and `query_profile` evidence captured through `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the SQLite acceptance database; never provision a second engine only for profiling. Read [capabilities/reports.md](capabilities/reports.md) whenever a page/API returns Report rows or offers Report export. If the delivery cannot prove the contracts, classify the in-scope Report list/export as `acceptance_failed` with a Runtime Report owner gap. Never substitute browser-memory pagination, repeated full-result execution per chunk, generic batch download, duplicate artifacts, a second query, invented infrastructure, or excluded scope. Before capability selection or model authoring, read [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md) completely and derive G01-G32 applicability from the current requirements/model demand pool. Re-read it during verify and close every applicable static plus real-Runtime proof; do not wait until terminal acceptance to discover a missing transaction, index, timeout, provider lifecycle, SSE resume, data-scope isolation or recovery contract. ## model ### Derive and reconcile resources Inspect the delivered frontend's typed API layer and Mock adapters read-only, together with the requirement documents. Extract every displayed/input/filtered/sorted/related field, query, report, operation, role, transition, transaction, permission, scope, approval, schedule, automation, notification, external effect, error/conflict contract, Identity menu entry, and role-menu assignment the frontend Mock contract or requirement expresses. Keep each demand's source and classification; do not turn a Mock assumption into model truth. - Object identity is the business entity. - Relation identity is source + field + target + cardinality. - Action identity is semantics + target + transition + transaction boundary. - Workflow and state-machine identity is the business lifecycle. - Assign one owner module to each canonical resource. - Merge compatible demands and union compatible field uses. - Report incompatible field, relation, transition, transaction, or role demands together. - Do not duplicate resources, use last-write-wins, or clone an Action because roles differ. - Configure menu definitions through the foundation Identity menu management boundary and assign them to roles there. ### Map accepted facts to capabilities Only after domain truth closes, prefer Runtime CRUD, standard record operations, state machine, Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, record views, Reports, and published Connector operations. Create project-owned Handler or Connector source only for a concrete capability gap that metadata cannot express. Platform capability decides this mapping, never the business fact. Before recording any platform owner gap, ensure the delivery-owned Runtime Client SDK and disclosure contract are materialized: when absent or invalid, run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project materialize runtime-client --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` with the batch's pinned Domainry Plane target. A fetch, signature, cache, receipt, or package failure is a delivery blocker; never fake, copy, alias, or bypass the SDK ([runtime-client.md](runtime-client.md)). Then discover platform capability through the fixed category index: `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-categories` once, then each selected `contract capability-category` batch once; register both levels plus the operation-to-endpoint mapping as TODO evidence and reconcile route, reuse classification, Surface projection, owner permission, data scope, and machine schema separately ([runtime-client.md](runtime-client.md)). Treat `operations_only` as an existing isolated capability, not backend absence. Agent task operations and diagnostics are operations-only even though authorized Business routes exist under `/agent-dialog/**`; never move or call the operations routes from project source. Reject unknown keys and never use free-text `contract search` for Admin capability discovery. ## apply ### Author the model files and release Close every module's Object, Relation, Action, Role, authorization, data scope, Workflow, state machine, Report, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, seed, and acceptance inventory before authoring the backend model files. Declare that complete inventory as items in `backend/model/*.json`, grouped by owning module — typically one file per module; the exact file contract lives in [backend-model.md](backend-model.md). Before the first `model validate`, close the cross-resource preflight and strict nested-shape card in [backend-model.md](backend-model.md): exact Identity menu/role-menu fields, `min`/`max` validation keys, array-valued report metrics, the exact Report emission/`object_sql_v1` card (`value.key`, alias-only join cardinalities, and bounded SQL), closed export-control fields, and bidirectional behavior/resource ownership. Partial-resource or intermediate-file validation is a guaranteed-invalid checkpoint and is prohibited. Repair the complete diagnostic batch before revalidating. After validation first reaches `state:"valid"`, freeze the model draft while recording evidence; a requirement-backed change starts a new atomic draft and requires `model validate` plus `model plan` again. The model files are the single backend authoring surface and the source of truth. Inspect the pending change set with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"`; bootstrap an older project once with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"`. Do not edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**` Ledger state by hand ([backend-model.md](backend-model.md)). When the module inventories are complete, release the Blueprint once: ```text "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [one pinned explicit --environment or --service target] ``` `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. The complete apply semantics — stage chaining, checklist gating, destructive refusal and `--allow-destructive`, rename = delete + create, receipt path, `--sync-only`, and the prohibition on direct Domainry Plane calls or split publish/materialize maintenance commands — are defined in [backend-model.md](backend-model.md). Always pass reviewed `--product-surfaces`; it is the backend-to-frontend integration boundary used by materialization, not authorization to generate or redesign page source. After a stage failure, repair the model files or reported input and rerun the same command. An existing delivery that returns `evolution_review_required` may rerun only with the emitted audit SHA-256 and reviewed reason. Backend materialization inside `model apply` installs backend templates, generated/source inputs, contracts, Runtime manifest, and Go dependencies. It must never create, modify, or delete `frontend/**`, including frontend paths contained in Project Source Seed. Backend materialization is not the local-composition compile closure. The project template may already call `composition.RuntimeOptions`, while `generated/composition/extensions.gen.go`, the Action registry, and the Connector registry remain owned by source finalization. Complete that closure only with `project source finalize`. ### Implement and integrate - Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project ` immediately after materialization. Treat the bounded envelope's Action key/path/state list as the Handler implementation inventory and retain the exact `.implementation_packet.path`, payload/file hashes, and delivery/materialization identity. The CLI atomically persists the complete content-addressed packet under managed `.domainry/builder/**`; never redirect stdout to create it and never use or invent `latest.json`. First inspect the envelope's small Action index, then use local `jq` for exactly one packet `actions[]` entry selected by `action_key` and only the referenced `documents[]` content selected by SHA. Never `cat` or print the complete packet, and do not issue one `action context` command per Action in the same installed batch. The command creates only missing canonical project-owned Handler/test skeletons, never replaces an existing file, and writes in bounded atomic batches. Use focused `action context` only for an isolated repair or an audit-bound pending evolution absent from the installed packet. - Compileability of a prepared skeleton proves only contract shape. Every prepared `*.not_implemented` result remains fail closed and must be replaced by accepted business behavior before source finalization can pass. - Obtain bounded coding context for approved source gaps. - Implement Handler, domain, Connector, and tests by module. Replace each generated placeholder test with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs plus current output/effect assertions; retain separate hand-written nil/authorization robustness tests when they remain valuable. - Use generated typed capabilities and real data access. - Reject placeholders, empty success returns, and handlers that never use their capability set. - Complete authorization, transaction, idempotency, audit, outbox, and errors.

# Domain truth and settlement

## Gate

Freeze business facts before capability discovery. Platform capabilities decide how accepted facts map to Runtime; they do not decide what the facts are.

| Kind | Meaning | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occurred fact | A completed business event and its event-time inputs, rules, and result | Persist when it occurs; correct by reversal or adjustment |
| Summary | A read-only aggregation of occurred facts | Use Dataset or native SQL; never own the formula that created the fact |
| Simulation | A hypothetical result under assumed inputs or rules | Isolate from official facts, ledgers, payroll, and reports |

For every material calculation, decide: Calculation Owner, Evaluation Time, Persisted Result, Policy/Rule Snapshot, Input Snapshot, Calculation Trace, Correction/Reversal Strategy, Downstream Consumers, and Report Source of Truth. Keep affected modeling blocked while any decision is open.

## Versioned settlement pattern

```text
Versioned Policy
  → Atomic Settlement Action
  → Calculation Snapshot
  → Immutable Ledger
  → Reversal / Adjustment
  → Native SQL Report
  → Server-paginated Consumers
  → Same-Report bounded threshold router (sync exhausted <=1000 / async on row 1001)
  → Async Terminal Notification
  → Payroll / Export Reconciliation
```

Use this pattern for an event that locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input. In one transaction, the settlement Action must validate idempotency and authorization, resolve the event-time policy, and persist policy identity/version, the actual rule snapshot, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, final result, immutable ledger entries, and audit/outbox effects. A later policy version affects only later events.

Never update or delete an original financial ledger entry to correct history. Append a linked reversal for cancellation/refund and a reasoned adjustment for an approved correction. Preserve `reversal_of` or equivalent lineage, the original ledger ID, actor, time, reason, and approval boundary. A locked payroll/export consumer records the ledger IDs or a governed scope/hash it consumed; later adjustments follow the explicit correction period instead of silently changing the locked result.

## Anti-patterns

- Repeating one formula across pages or several reports.
- Joining current Settings to recompute a historical financial result.
- Rendering absent or unproven facts as numeric zero.
- Giving summary, detail, page, payroll, and export different scopes or formulas.
- Allowing Settings changes to drift historical results.
- Omitting ledger-ID-level traceability across consumers.
- Building a project-specific report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator.
- Returning an unbounded list or fetching all rows for browser-memory pagination.
- Bypassing the fixed 1000-row router, using a second export-only query, or producing duplicate artifacts for an equivalent canonical fingerprint.
- Completing or failing an export without a notification linked to its audit, job, and artifact, or allowing an unaudited/unexpired-but-out-of-scope download.

## Acceptance matrix

Cover applicable boundaries with event-time input, policy identity, snapshot/ledger IDs, trace, consumer result, and allow/deny evidence:

- policy version switch before/after effective time;
- business-day cutoff and cross-midnight events;
- multi-party allocation with deterministic remainder handling;
- full/partial refund and reversal lineage;
- correction after payroll or another consumer is locked;
- summary/detail/page/payroll/export reconciliation by ledger ID;
- cross-store and cross-entity permission/data-scope denial;
- Runtime restart and Settings change without historical drift.
- maximum-page enforcement and stable cursor traversal without duplicate or missing rows, including equal sort keys;
- explicit `truncated` and exact/estimated/omitted `total` semantics;
- exact permission-filtered totals at 0, 1000, and 1001 with synchronous/asynchronous routing and identical Report/parameters/source/Scope;
- concurrent, running, completed, expired, failed/cancelled, source-change and Scope-change fingerprint replay semantics;
- asynchronous completed and failed terminal notifications linked to export audit/job/artifact, plus requester/Scope/expiry/integrity/audit download denial.
