## Read models, errors, and application composition

After a mutation, invalidate the current workspace-and-Surface read-model root by default. Use narrower object/report invalidation only when the page can name every affected read model. Never leave mutation success visible beside stale business data.

Never invent a synthetic `system.refresh` Action. A refresh control re-runs its protected query and exposes `mutation_refresh`; it calls a business Action only when that exact Action is declared by the current Runtime manifest.

Do not render `permission_denied`, hidden scope, concurrency conflict, or business rejection as empty data. Clear or hide the prior live snapshot before entering loading/error/denied/unauthenticated state; never leave old totals, cards, records, hardcoded scenario proof, or optimistic success copy beside a failure. Render the stable `RuntimeApiError` category and retain its code and request ID in diagnostic evidence. Permission-based route/action pruning is presentation policy and never replaces an allowed/denied Runtime request in security proof.

The Runtime client does not invent industry view models. Project source owns which declared objects, reports, and Actions compose each page; table columns, chart mappings, workflow presentation, role-specific flows, and route-specific loading, empty, error, denied, retry, and responsive states.

## Managed Runtime proof

Start with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process start --project <project> --bundle <path> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>` (the default is `127.0.0.1:8081`; use an explicit free loopback port for isolated evaluation or concurrent projects), inspect with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process status --project <project>`, and stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project <project>`. The managed receipt records the chosen address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Do not background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, or kill unrelated processes.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) — do pure selection into a bounded slice first, then process with bounded unrolled steps or a batch/query capability; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Minimal accepted shape for fan-out writes:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
// Bounded unrolled processing: one indexed helper call per capacity slot,
// each a no-op past len(pending); capability I/O lives only inside the helper.
if state, err = processAt(ctx, caps, pending, 0, state); err != nil {
    return out, err
}
if state, err = processAt(ctx, caps, pending, 1, state); err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// ... one literal line per slot up to runCapacity-1
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `project source finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so the wrapper below is the command to bind as Gate evidence):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). The development TODO template carries this as a required implementation-stage checkbox — bind it with `... run <gate-id> --bind source --` followed by the command above verbatim (it already starts with `bash -c`).

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty — but the generated typed record bindings currently drop the `Version`/`UpdatedAt` that `runtimeext.Record` carries, so no typed accessor exists. Until the SDK exposes the record version, pass the command's idempotency identity (e.g. the `request_id`) as the subject version and record the platform gap; do not leave the field empty and do not skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.

- **Every project-owned Handler Action — including scheduler-driven bulk handlers — must declare at least one required payload field in `idempotency_keys`** (`ledger.action_idempotency_required`). A scheduled job's invocation payload carries the key (e.g. a required `run_date` bound from the trigger event).
- **Multiple `data_permissions[]` entries for the same object do NOT merge**: the validator reads one entry's `read`/`write` per object, so "read=department + write=own" cannot be expressed as two entries (`ledger.action_role_data_permission_required` reports the losing entry's booleans). Declare a single entry with the union capability and enforce the narrower write constraint through a before-update automation assert on the owner, a Handler precondition, or CRUD permission removal.

## Single ownership

Every rendered resource key has exactly one originating model item. A `ledger.resource_duplicate` diagnostic means a second item attempted to emit an existing resource; it is never an overlay or merge mechanism. Repair it in the model files: remove the duplicate declaration and extend the item that already owns the resource. For example, a missing permission on an emitted role belongs in the item that already emits the role, not in a new `actor_role` item emitting the same role key.

Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior; the exact owner-to-emitted-collection mapping and resource-key rules live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md) — do not guess a collection from prose.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model validate|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model validate` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `project acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model validate` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
- **Denied report cases are auto-derived — never author them.** A scenario referencing a report in `expected_reports` must use a role that IS allowed to read it (`acceptance.report_role_not_allowed` otherwise). For a protected report (non-empty `audience_roles`/`required_permissions`), the builder automatically finds an unauthorized role and emits the `permission_denied` case itself; it fails `acceptance.report_denied_role_missing` if no declared role is unauthorized. The same auto-derivation applies to Workflow denied cases.
- **CRUD/list/navigation coverage uses `config.runtime_operations` route keys** from the pinned Runtime Domain API `routes` map. The most-used keys: `object_query` (bounded list GET /objects/{objectKey}/records), `object_detail`, `object_create` (idempotency-key required), `object_update`, `object_delete`, `object_action`, `record_action`, `record_export`, `record_import_apply`, `effective_menu_list` (GET /identity/effective-menus), `business_notification_list`/`business_notification_stream` (SSE). Verify a key's readiness through `contract capability-category` before relying on it.
- **Prepare prerequisites**: a current verification receipt, a running healthy managed Runtime of the exact current cohort, and the runtime-client SDK materialized. Pass `--project` as an **absolute path** — a relative path currently fails the database-identity check with `managed Runtime database identity escapes the current project`.

Their nested shapes are closed too. `expected_records[]` accepts only `object_key`, `record_key`, `field_key`, `state`, `count`, and `values`; it has no `scope`. `expected_reports[]` accepts only `report_key`, `expected_run`, `expected_export`, `filters`, and array-valued `metrics` (use `[]`, not `{}`, when no metric is asserted). Assertions accept only their published typed assertion fields.

When a requirement consumes a typed Runtime capability that is not already represented by `actions`, `workflows`, or `expected_reports`, declare it under the scenario's `config.runtime_operations`. Each entry uses only `route_key` from the pinned Runtime Domain API plus optional `case`, `lifecycle`, `restart_sensitive`, `expected_outcome`, and `expected_error_code`; unknown fields, wrong field types, and route keys absent from the pinned Runtime Domain API fail during `model validate` (`evidence.typed_operation_route_unknown`). Use separate positive and `permission_denied` scenarios/roles for a write. The acceptance denominator resolves the route to the unified capability disclosure, preserves its real read/write effect class, required permissions, and SSE disposition, and rejects an allowed role labeled denied, a positive role missing the published permission, or a write without both positive and denied coverage. `expected_outcome`, when supplied, is one of `passed`, `denied`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `concealed`, `not_found`, or `failed`. For an SSE route, the case/lifecycle must be `sse_disconnect_resume`/`disconnect_resume` and `restart_sensitive` must be omitted or `false`: Last-Event-ID reconnect is not a managed process restart and requires only the stream transcript plus durable refetch. Do not reduce it to a connection-open check or attach unrelated restart/audit evidence.

```json
{"config": {
  "runtime_operations": [
    {"route_key":"business_notification_stream","case":"sse_disconnect_resume","lifecycle":"disconnect_resume"}
  ]
}}
```

A positive scenario's referenced seed records must already satisfy every source-owned Handler precondition needed for the expected success path. Every positive or denied role used by executable acceptance must have a project-declared `demo_users[]` identity. Bind a specific identity through `actor`; when an automatic standard case only has a role, that role must have exactly one demo user or exactly one user marked `acceptance_default:true`. The default applies across both `role_key` and `role_keys`; alphabetical order is never identity resolution. A role label alone is not a login. Keep separate negative business-precondition scenarios when that rejection matters. Denied authorization scenarios remain distinct and must fail at the Runtime authorization boundary.

When a positive Action needs a value the standard runner cannot derive, declare the runner-owned fixture in that scenario's open `config` map: `"action_payloads":[{"action_key":"<declared scenario action>","fields":{"<payload key>":{"value":<typed scalar>}}}]`. An omitted `encoding` requires a literal conforming exactly to the declared scalar payload type; relation/reference literals accept only `$record:<seed-key>` of the declared target, and user literals accept only `$actor`. The existing `{"encoding":"json","value":<array or object>}` form remains available only for `text`/`long_text`, resolving nested `$record:<seed-key>` values before canonical JSON encoding. The Action must belong to that positive scenario, actor plus Action must identify one scenario/role binding, and malformed, missing-seed, duplicate, or ambiguous fixtures fail closed; fixture fields are never conflict-mutation slots. Do not declare fixtures for values the standard type derivation already supplies.

Validation must close actor/role, object/relation, Action/authorization/data access, Automation/Workflow/Scheduler ownership, frontend entrypoints, and positive plus denied acceptance. ## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) — do pure selection into a bounded slice first, then process with bounded unrolled steps or a batch/query capability; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Minimal accepted shape for fan-out writes:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
// Bounded unrolled processing: one indexed helper call per capacity slot,
// each a no-op past len(pending); capability I/O lives only inside the helper.
if state, err = processAt(ctx, caps, pending, 0, state); err != nil {
    return out, err
}
if state, err = processAt(ctx, caps, pending, 1, state); err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// ... one literal line per slot up to runCapacity-1
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `project source finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so the wrapper below is the command to bind as Gate evidence):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). The development TODO template carries this as a required implementation-stage checkbox — bind it with `... run <gate-id> --bind source --` followed by the command above verbatim (it already starts with `bash -c`).

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty — but the generated typed record bindings currently drop the `Version`/`UpdatedAt` that `runtimeext.Record` carries, so no typed accessor exists. Until the SDK exposes the record version, pass the command's idempotency identity (e.g. the `request_id`) as the subject version and record the platform gap; do not leave the field empty and do not skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.

# Reports

> **TL;DR** — Owns: object analytics/Reports, `object_sql_v1` authoring, bounded pagination and threshold routing, governed export, fingerprint replay. Read when: a page or API returns Report rows or offers Report export. Never: unbounded/browser pagination or a separate count-only query.

## Problem and owner
Runtime report capability owns governed Dataset summary/snapshot and restricted `object_sql_v1` query/export boundaries.

Reports consume accepted domain facts; they do not decide or recreate those facts. Complete the domain-truth Gate before choosing an execution form.

| Demand | Required design |
| --- | --- |
| Simple single-object or fixed-dimension aggregation | Governed Dataset |
| Complex JOIN, CTE, window function, or special aggregation | Author-written native SQL file; use `object_sql_v1` only when the active Runtime supports every required construct, otherwise record a Report Runtime owner gap |
| Checkout, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll locking | Atomic Action + Calculation Snapshot + immutable Ledger first; Report only aggregates those facts |
| Hypothetical rule or parameter trial | Separate Simulation; never write into official Reports or ledgers |

Never build a project-specific Report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator. Runtime's internal parsing and semantic binding are security implementation details, not an authoring surface. Never make a Report join current Settings to replay historical financial calculations.

Current compatibility boundary: `sql_file` improves source ownership but does not widen `object_sql_v1`. The current P0 Runtime accepts bounded SELECT/JOIN/GROUP BY/HAVING/ORDER BY and rejects author CTEs, subqueries, UNION, and windows. When a truthful report needs a rejected construct, keep it as an explicit Runtime Report owner gap; do not force it into Dataset, rewrite the domain facts, or claim the Skill supports unrestricted native SQL. The follow-up platform owner is Runtime Report authoring/execution and must preserve permission, RLS, read-only execution, parameter binding, resource limits, export-scope parity, and source-file hash provenance.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Every Report declares exactly one execution definition: a governed `dataset`, or `object_sql_v1` with canonical SQL, declared source objects, typed parameters, result schema, optional join cardinalities, and timeout. In `backend/model/*.json`, native SQL uses one matching `sql_file:"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"` instead of inline `sql`; the V2 model loader normalizes and hashes that project-owned file and embeds it into the same published `sql` contract. Frontends consume only the corresponding typed Runtime Client operation; Object SQL never falls back to Dataset or browser/in-memory evaluation.

## List pagination and export lifecycle

These are non-negotiable Report design Gates: bounded server pagination for list rows; one permission-filtered bounded threshold probe of the identical Report contract; fixed export routing at 1000; terminal exact total; atomic canonical-fingerprint replay; and requester-only completed/failed Inbox notification for the asynchronous branch. Close them before selecting Report metadata or implementation.

Any Report response that returns list rows must expose bounded server pagination. Its thin contract names either the platform standard or `page_size` plus an opaque `cursor`, the maximum page size, a deterministic stable sort and stable cursor with a unique tie-breaker bound into the cursor, and explicit `truncated` and `total` semantics. A valid observable tie-breaker may be one unique dimension in ascending or descending order, or the complete strictly monotonic dimension tuple; repeated or order-reversing tuples are not proof. `total` may be exact, estimated, or omitted, but the response and PRD must say which. `truncated` distinguishes a bounded partial result from an exhausted result. Never return an unbounded list, fetch all rows into the browser, or call slicing in browser memory “pagination.”

Every Report export prepare must probe the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed routing threshold is 1000: an exhausted bounded probe from 0 through 1000 yields the exact total and returns the synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 is sufficient to enqueue the asynchronous export-job substrate without a separate `COUNT(*)` or full materialization. The worker reads the same Report contract in bounded database pages and records the final exact total at terminal completion. Only the async completed/failed terminal transitions publish requester-only Inbox notifications linked through the job to export audit and artifact. Both branches keep governed artifact/download reauthorization, expiry, integrity, and audit. A worker that reruns the full Report for every output page does not satisfy this contract.

Server deduplication is mandatory and does not rely on UI debounce or caller-generated randomness. Canonical fingerprint inputs include Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and the frozen result version. Exclude `audit_id`: it records one request but does not change the exported result. When an equivalent click supplies a new audit, atomically link and close that audit against the original job/artifact; do not return an idempotency conflict, create another job/file/download, or emit another terminal notification. Database compare-and-create ensures concurrent equivalent requests return one identity. An accepted/running fingerprint returns its existing job. A completed fingerprint with an unexpired, intact, currently authorized artifact reuses that artifact/download. Failed/cancelled work, expired/corrupt artifacts, or a changed SQL/source/parameter/authorization Scope may create exactly one new execution.

Current transport surface: `GET /reports/{reportKey}/summary` and `POST /reports/{reportKey}/query` accept `page_size` plus an opaque cursor and return `page_size`, `next_cursor`, `truncated`, `total`, and `total_semantics`; the hard maximum is 200. `total_semantics` is `at_least` while a bounded page proves only a lower bound and becomes `exact` when traversal is exhausted. `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare` returns `200` for the governed synchronous artifact or `202 Accepted` plus `Location` for a requester-owned job; job status/cancel and governed download routes are published. This describes request and response shape only. Verify the active package separately for bounded execution, query-count and memory budgets, signed source-version/keyset cursor behavior, restart recovery, no duplicate/missing rows, replay, download reauthorization, and terminal notification.

Async reauthorization is part of that supported contract, not an implementation detail projects may bypass. Before page one and again at governed download, Runtime restores the job workspace into Identity context, resolves the current persisted user-role assignment and organization facts, resolves the same default business-profile facts used by HTTP prepare, and compares the frozen authorization/data-Scope hash. A manifest-only role, missing workspace context, or invented Product/Business Surface is not equivalent. True permission, assignment, organization, or business-profile drift fails closed; unchanged facts must not fail merely because execution moved from HTTP to a worker.

Governed export uses `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare`
with `audit_id` plus an immutable `scope`. The scope may name only declared
report dimension keys, measure keys, and analysis keys; it binds query identity,
filters, date dimension/range, IANA timezone, stable tag-family values plus their
`any|all` relation, projected result fields,
purpose, metric definition key/version assertions, freshness, and optional
current role/data-scope assertions. Runtime canonicalizes role, data scopes, and
metric definition versions from the authenticated principal and current report.
Unknown dimensions/operators/fields, arbitrary query fragments, mismatched
assertions, masked measures, and stale snapshot requirements fail closed.
`query_key` is executable only when it names one `dataset.query_predicates[]`
entry and `tags` may name only `dataset.tag_predicates[]` entries. Each entry is
a stable `key` plus 1..16 closed dataset `filters`; arbitrary SQL, expressions,
field names, or operators are never accepted from the request. Selected tag
predicates are canonicalized, deduplicated, sorted, and combined with AND. The
summary endpoint accepts the same `query_key` and repeated `tags` parameters so
the visible page and prepared CSV execute one predicate contract. Governed
export additionally requires every selected key in the matching control's
`allowed_query_keys` or `allowed_tags`; empty control allowlists grant nothing.
Unknown keys/tags/operators and snapshot selector overrides fail closed. A realtime request timezone is
executable: date-only bounds are converted from that IANA timezone to exact UTC
instants and time buckets use the same scoped timezone. Snapshot exports reject
a timezone override that differs from the report snapshot definition.

The published Prepare route performs the bounded authorized threshold probe and
binds the result identity. An exhausted 0-through-1000-row probe synchronously
persists and returns the governed CSV (zero rows produce the valid header-only
artifact); observing row 1001 returns the requester-owned job. The current
Runtime bounded path pushes `LIMIT page_size+1` plus a hard result maximum into
supported Dataset and `object_sql_v1` execution, appends deterministic tie
terms, signs the authorized source version into continuation cursors, and
rejects stale cursors instead of silently duplicating or omitting rows. The
async worker fences that source version, commits immutable chunks with its
checkpoint, and resumes without re-running a complete Report or calling prepare
again. Unsupported complex Dataset shapes fail closed with
`backend.report.bounded_page_unavailable`; a declared hard maximum may use full
execution only when it is at most the synchronous threshold, never for an async
claim. Active-delivery `pagination_trace`, SQLite `query_profile` (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`),
restart and artifact evidence remain mandatory. Watermarking remains governed
when configured.
The synchronous response carries artifact/content-hash headers; a completed
asynchronous job exposes its artifact ID, download token, expiry, and content
hash. `content_sha256` is SHA-256 of the exact final bytes returned by
`GET /report-exports/downloads/{token}`. Every download rechecks the
requester/workspace, expiry, current report/control/object/field permission,
authorization/data-scope fingerprint, definition hashes, immutable scope hash,
and file hash, and audits success, denial, or expiry. A project Action's legacy
`download_id` or metadata `content_hash` is not a Runtime download token or file
hash; continue the handoff through prepare and use only its returned token/hash.
The audit Action creates only a request record in a prepare-eligible status such
as `requested`. `record_mapping` declares the accepted request statuses plus the
Runtime-owned prepared/downloaded/denied/expired status values and audit
row-count/scope-hash fields. Runtime writes prepared status, actual grouped CSV
row count, and `sha256:<normalized-scope-hash>` in one record update only after
governed artifact bytes exist; it never trusts a client-provided filters hash.
Download success writes downloaded, rejected prepare writes denied, and an
expired token writes expired. Zero rows are a successful synchronous export,
not a denial.

The route surface is not proof of production execution semantics. If Report list or export is in the frozen requirement scope, it cannot be marked not applicable or silently excluded: the active delivery must pass the bounded execution, stable-cursor, SQLite query-profile and recovery cases; otherwise acceptance fails with the exact Runtime Report owner gap. If no Report list/export requirement exists, record the machine-derived not-applicable reason.

The Blueprint shape is exact. A Report emission repeats the same key in both places: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`; the emission envelope never supplies the required `value.key` for the SQL-file loader. A report value has top-level `key`, optional `name`/`i18n`, exactly one of `dataset` or `object_sql_v1`, and optional `required_permissions`, `audience_roles`, `evidence_requirements`, `materialization`, and `export_scope`. Dataset-owned fields must be nested under `dataset`: `source`, `joins`, `filters`, `query_predicates`, `tag_predicates`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `time_grain`, `time_zone`, `sort`, `limit`, `privacy`, `comparisons`, and `analyses`. Object SQL owns `sql`, `source_objects`, `parameters`, `result_schema`, `join_cardinalities`, and `timeout_milliseconds`. Do not put `object_key`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `filters`, `allowed_roles`, `description`, `snapshot_policy`, or `export_policy` at report top level.

Call `queryReportObjectSQL(reportKey, parameters, {pageSize, cursor})` for interactive Object SQL and continue only with the returned opaque `next_cursor`. Governed export passes the same declared values as `prepareReportExportRouted(..., {scope: {parameters, purpose, freshness:{mode:'realtime'}, ...}})`. Runtime canonicalizes defaults/types before scope hashing and audit, compiles the same SQL, injects the same RLS, checks the same read fields plus export permission, and reauthorizes on download. The preparing principal's role additionally needs `report_export_audit.update`, `report_export_download.create`, and data write permission on both the declared `audit_object` and `download_object`; grant these at model time or prepare fails 403. Dataset selectors (`query_key`, tags, filters, date range, analysis, timezone, metrics) are invalid for Object SQL; unknown parameters, arbitrary SQL, fields, or result columns fail closed. Keep deprecated `prepareReportExport`/`exportReportObject` only so previously generated adapters compile; never author new calls to them.

`dataset.source` requires both `object_key` and a non-empty local `alias`. A dimension requires `key` and `field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. A measure requires `key` and `operation`; legal operations are `count`, `distinct_count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `ratio`, `duration`, and `percentile`. A plain count needs no field. Field-based measures use `field`, not `field_key` or `aggregation`. Every alias referenced by fields and measures must be the source alias or a declared join alias.

A join keeps the legacy single-key form `left_field` + `right_field`, or uses
`field_equalities` with 1..8 unique `{left_field,right_field}` pairs; never mix
the two forms. Every pair is equality-only, references the join's `left_alias`
and joined `alias`, and requires the same read/export field checks and indexing
as a single-key join. `cardinality` remains required. Runtime rejects actual
right-key duplication for `many_to_one`, duplication on either side for
`one_to_one`, and plan-time additive-measure amplification across
`one_to_many`; it never silently aggregates a cardinality violation.

Every Object field used by a report join, filter, time-bucket dimension, or analysis entity/time/event field must be indexed. Set `"config":{"indexed":true}` on the declared Object field unless it is already `unique:true`; relation fields are indexed by default unless explicitly disabled. Runtime's physical recommendation is tenant-leading `workspace_id,<field_key>`. Dataset-level `time_grain` is a default for every dimension that omits its own grain, so do not set it on a dataset containing categorical dimensions such as `status`, `result`, or `method`; put `time_grain` only on the actual datetime dimension. Otherwise those categorical fields become time-bucket access paths and must also be indexed.

Omit `dataset.privacy` unless the report truly needs group suppression. When present, it is a closed object with exactly `minimum_group_size` (integer 2..1000) and `entity_field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. The entity field must exist on the named dataset source/join alias and identifies the distinct privacy subject counted for suppression. `mask_sensitive_fields` is not a report privacy property; field masking remains owned by Runtime CLS and export policy.

`report_export_controls[]` is also closed. Use `masking_required` for the export masking flag, never `mask_sensitive_fields`. Its declared fields are `key`, `name`, `i18n`, `report_key`, `source_objects`, `sensitive_source_objects`, `sensitive_field_policy_keys`, `object_export_policy_keys`, `approval_required`, `masking_required`, `watermark`, `audit_object`, `download_object`, `record_mapping`, `export_action`, `allowed_query_keys`, `allowed_tags`, `max_rows`, `reason`, and optional `config`. Required `record_mapping` keys are `audit_report_key_field`, `audit_requester_field`, `audit_status_field`, `audit_prepared_statuses`, `audit_prepared_status`, `audit_downloaded_status`, `audit_denied_status`, `audit_expired_status`, `audit_row_count_field`, `audit_scope_hash_field`, `download_audit_field`, `download_filename_field`, `download_content_hash_field`, and `download_expires_at_field`; token/watermark/download-number field mappings are optional.

Preflight export authorization as one requesting principal, not as grants spread across roles. At least one role must simultaneously have the Report audience and required permissions, the export Action grant, `<source>.export` plus source data read for every source Object, `<audit_object>.update` plus audit data write, and `<download_object>.create` plus download data write. Also give the emitted `export_action` a matching `business_handler` behavior owner; governance/helper Actions are not exempt from reverse behavior ownership.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use Runtime reports for governed analytics. Do not fetch all records into the browser, paginate in browser memory, or bypass export permissions. The legitimate synchronous `<=1000` prepare response is Runtime-governed; it is not permission to create CSV in the browser or call the removed backing-record route. Do not use generic batch download, add a second query, vary the threshold, or generate another artifact for an equivalent fingerprint.

Summary, detail, page, payroll, and export must share the same authoritative facts and permission/data scope. Do not repeat formulas in any consumer, zero-fill a missing/unproven fact, or omit ledger-ID-level traceability where a ledger exists. Settings changes must not drift historical results.

## Examples
Correct minimal governed summary:

```json
{
  "key":"member_status_summary","name":"Member status summary",
  "dataset":{
    "source":{"object_key":"gym_member","alias":"member"},
    "dimensions":[{"key":"status","field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"status"}}],
    "measures":[{"key":"members","operation":"count","source_alias":"member"}]
  },
  "audience_roles":["gym_manager"],
  "required_permissions":["gym_member.read"],
  "evidence_requirements":[{"object_key":"gym_member","minimum_records":1,"required_non_empty_fields":["status"]}],
  "materialization":{"maximum_lag_seconds":300,"consistency_retries":3}
}
```

Wrong: `{"object_key":"gym_member","dimensions":[{"field_key":"status"}],"measures":[{"aggregation":"count"}],"allowed_roles":["gym_manager"]}`. Those are not the Runtime Report contract. Wrong: unrestricted CSV from a custom endpoint; use governed report export.

If a truthful business requirement needs a Report result cap, `dataset.limit` may declare that cap, but it is never pagination evidence and must not be set to 1000 merely because export routing uses a 1000-row threshold.

Correct privacy fragment: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":2,"entity_field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"member_no"}}`. Wrong: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":0,"entity_field":"member_no","mask_sensitive_fields":true}`.

Correct indexed report field: `{"key":"occurred_at","name":"Occurred at","type":"datetime","required":true,"config":{"indexed":true}}`, used by `{"key":"day","field":{"source_alias":"access","field_key":"occurred_at"},"time_grain":"day"}`. Wrong: a dataset-level `"time_grain":"day"` shared by categorical `result` and `method` dimensions.

Correct compound current-version join: `{"alias":"current_version","object_key":"order_version","type":"inner","left_alias":"order","field_equalities":[{"left_field":"id","right_field":"order_id"},{"left_field":"version_counter","right_field":"version_no"}],"cardinality":"one_to_one"}`. Wrong: keeping only the ID equality and filtering a version number from a different alias, which can amplify unrelated versions.

## Authority and limits
Owners: `internal/runtime/domain/report/contract/report_authoring.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/report/service/report_domain_service.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/report/service/report_snapshot_service.go`.

## object_sql_v1 authoring contract (validated against the shipped compiler)

The SQL is compiled by a **vitess (MySQL-dialect) parser** with a closed plan contract; every rule below fails `model validate` (`backend.report.object_sql_*`). The parser dialect governs authoring syntax only — execution and acceptance run on the managed Runtime's database (SQLite in acceptance); never provision another database engine for this:

- **Reserved identifiers need backticks**: an object named `lead`, `order`, `group`, etc. collides with MySQL keywords — write ``FROM `lead` AS l``. Double quotes are NOT identifier quotes in this dialect.
- **Exactly one joined source tree**, and **every FROM/JOIN source requires an explicit alias** (`FROM `lead` AS l`). Each joined alias (not the root alias) needs exactly one `join_cardinalities` contract entry with the closed shape `{"alias":"joined_alias","cardinality":"many_to_one"}`. Only `alias` and `cardinality` are allowed; `left_alias`/`right_alias` belong to Dataset joins and are invalid here.
- **Every SELECT column requires an explicit alias that exactly equals the corresponding `result_schema[i].key`**, in order, no `SELECT *`: `SELECT l.company_name AS company_name, ...`.
- **`result_schema` entries require BOTH `type` and `kind`**. `kind` is `dimension` or `measure`. `type` is the closed enum `text`, `integer`, `number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `currency` — object field types such as `phone`, `user`, `relation`, `select` are NOT result types; declare them as `text` in the result schema (the object field declaration is unaffected).
- Declared `source_objects` must exactly cover the objects referenced in FROM/JOINs; the declared column type must be compatible with the compiled expression type.
- **Declare an explicit `ORDER BY` plus a literal `LIMIT` in `1..10000`** sized to the business bound: the compiled query otherwise applies a default `LIMIT 1000`, which equals the 1000/1001 sync/async export threshold, so a >1000-row report silently truncates to exactly 1000 rows in a synchronous export (database-agnostic rule). Values above 10000 fail `backend.report.object_sql_limit_invalid`; do not use a large placeholder.

Validated minimal example:

```sql
SELECT l.company_name AS company_name, l.expected_amount AS expected_amount
FROM `lead` AS l
ORDER BY l.id
LIMIT 5000
```

with `"result_schema": [{"key":"company_name","type":"text","kind":"dimension"},{"key":"expected_amount","type":"currency","kind":"measure"}]`.

# S1 Benchmark:内部工单系统(Ticketing)需求规格

本文档是 benchmark 的唯一需求输入,交给被评估 agent 作为「explicit current user requirement」。评分对照 `golden-checklist.json`,agent 不可见该文件。

## 业务背景

公司内部 IT 支持团队需要一个工单系统。员工通过客服录入工单,客服处理,主管监督并关单。

## 角色

- **support_agent(客服)**:创建工单、处理自己名下的工单、添加处理记录。只能看到分派给自己的工单。
- **support_manager(主管)**:查看全部工单、分派工单、关闭工单、查看统计报表。

## 功能需求

### 工单管理
1. 工单字段:标题(必填)、描述、优先级(low/medium/high/urgent)、状态、处理人(客服)、报告人姓名、创建/更新时间。
2. 工单状态机:`new → in_progress → resolved → closed`;`resolved` 可被打回 `in_progress`(reopen)。状态只能沿定义的转换变化,不允许跳转。
3. 客服可创建工单(初始状态 new)、更新自己名下工单的标题/描述/优先级。
4. 主管可将工单分派给任一客服;分派后处理人收到站内通知。
5. 开始处理(new → in_progress)与标记解决(in_progress → resolved)由该工单的处理人执行。
6. **只有主管可以关闭工单**(resolved → closed);客服尝试关闭必须被拒绝。
7. 主管可将 resolved 的工单重新打开(reopen → in_progress)。
8. 工单创建必须幂等:携带相同幂等键的重复提交只创建一条工单。

### 处理记录
9. 每条工单下可追加处理记录(comment):内容、记录人、时间;与工单为一对多关系。处理记录不可修改、不可删除。

### 权限与数据域
10. 客服的工单列表、详情、更新、状态操作都只能触达「处理人 = 自己」的工单;越权访问他人工单必须被拒绝(行级)。
11. 主管可见全部工单。
12. 所有状态变化必须留有审计记录。

### 报表
13. 主管可查看「按状态统计工单数」报表;客服无权查看。
14. 工单列表必须有界分页(服务端分页,禁止一次性返回全量)。

### 导航与验收
15. 两个角色登录 Business Workspace 后,各自菜单只出现自己有权使用的入口(客服:我的工单;主管:全部工单、报表)。

## 验收数据要求

提供两个角色的非人类验收身份与最小种子数据(至少 3 条不同状态、不同处理人的工单),保证上述每条需求都能在真实 Runtime 上执行验证。

## 范围限定

- 仅 Business Workspace,单 Surface;无 Consumer Portal、无外部连接器、无定时任务。
- 后端 + 平台能力实现;无自定义前端工作。

# Domainry Plane boundary

V2 uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `model apply` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, materializes or evolves the backend, and finalizes source. For an existing Builder delivery change, inspect the first run's immutable evolution audit, then rerun the same command with `--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>`. A stale audit fails closed. Repair any other failed input or stage and rerun the same command.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `model apply`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete backend project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. `frontend/**` remains read-only under every `Frontend mutation scope` (the scope records authorization context only): evidence that assigns a defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. Never edit `frontend/**`, `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.
